paragraphs.text: Across all 5 active Southwest Airlines cabin configurations (LOPAs), row numbering is standardized so that overwing emergency exits fall in the Row 14–16 band regardless of fuselage length. Every seat maps into three commercial tiers—Extra Legroom (ELR), Preferred, and Standard—with structural cutouts, windowless fuselage frames, and FAA-mandated recline locks varying by interior generation.

paragraphs.text: 1. Boeing 737-700 (73G — 137 Seats, 2026 Retrofit)
The single-overwing-exit 737-700 skips Rows 10–13 entirely so that its single exit row aligns at Row 15.

paragraphs.text: 2. Boeing 737-800 (738) & 737 MAX 8 (7M8-1) — "Heart" / Pre-Oct 2025 Cabins (175 Seats)
Both the legacy 737-800 Heart retrofit and pre-October 2025 737 MAX 8 deliveries share an identical 46 ELR / 45 Preferred / 84 Standard seat distribution across Rows 1–30.

paragraphs.text: 3. Boeing 737-800 (738-2) & 737 MAX 8 (7M8-2) — 2025 "Elevate" Cabins (175 Seats)
